description: A destructive action artifact is valid when every action is risk-classified, confirms intent with the user, cannot auto-confirm, provides undo capability when reversible, and links to a recovery path for high-risk outcomes.

rules.description: destructive-action-spec.json must exist with an actions array. Destructive features without a spec have undefined safety guarantees.
The actions array must not be empty. A destructive action compiler with no actions has nothing to enforce.
Every action riskLevel must be low, medium, high, or critical. Unmapped risk levels cannot trigger the appropriate safety rails.
Critical actions must declare requiresTextConfirmation:true. Clicking a button is insufficient confirmation for irreversible high-stakes operations.
Every action must have a confirmation object with a message string. The exception (confirmationNotRequired:true) is only valid for low-risk actions.
autoConfirm:true is forbidden on all actions regardless of risk level. Automatic confirmation bypasses user awareness and intent.
Every action with reversible:true must declare undoWindow (positive number of seconds) and undoTrigger (string). Reversibility without an undo mechanism is not reversibility.
undoWindow must not exceed 300 seconds (5 minutes). Longer windows create backend complexity and false expectations of safety.
Actions with riskLevel=high or critical must declare a recoveryPath string. After the undo window closes, users need to know where to go for recovery options.
All action ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate ids create ambiguous audit trails and confirmation dialog routing.
